newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures advance on jobs data, technicals.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures advance on jobs data, technicals.

text.p: U.S. debt futures opened an abbreviated trading session firmer and rose, assisted by technicals, to hefty gains when U.S. jobs payrolls proved somewhat weaker-than-forecast last month.
CBOT financial contracts will close at 1210 CDT/1710 GMT, Thursday, and CME interest-rate products will close at 1200 CDT/1700 GMT. All pits are shut Friday, July 4.

Nonfarm payrolls in June rose 217,000 versus forecasts for up 222,000. May's original 138,000-job rise was revised to a 166,000 rise. Joblessness last month rose to 5.0-percent compared with forecasts for a steady, 4.8-percent rate.
Average hourly earnings rose 0.3 percent to $12.22 versus forecasts for up 0.4 percent, while the workweek increased to 34.7 hours compared with forecasts for a 34.6-hour week.
Floor brokers tied the market's rally to the payrolls, jobless rate, and hourly earnings data plus technicals.
"That would do it," said one floor broker of the hourly earnings and jobless rate headline figures.

"It's a little bit surprising," said Jim Collins, senior vice president, Smith Barney. "Clearly the fact that the unemployment rate ticked up to the magical five-percent level has a lot to do with where we (bonds) are now."

He said although the other figures in the report were not too far out of line with forecasts, the recent debate about the concept of the non-accelerating inflation rate of unemployment had redoubled focus on the level of joblessness.

"The fact that we don't have a four (percent) handle on the unemployment rate is important," Collins added, saying the market already might be thinking the Fed would leave rates steady at its August policymaking meeting as well.
Futures had closed stronger Wednesday after the Federal Open Market Committee matched most pundits' forecasts and left short-term interest rates unchanged.
Technically, brokers said the September T-bonds staged an upside breakout as they cleared key resistance, including 112-08/32 and the June 20 high at 112-24/32.

Some now looked for a move soon to at least 114-00, especially if futures closed at these heights. But Collins wondered whether buyers who entered during Thursday's early runup would hold onto positions over the long holiday weekend or bail out by Thursday's early futures close.

At 0844 CDT/1344 GMT, Sept bond rose 1-05/32 to 113-07/32, notes gained 23/32 to 109-05/32, munis rose 1-00 to 118-23/32, Dec Euros rose 0.085 to 94.050, T-bills rose 0.075 at 94.720. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
